note: Hebrew matsevah is an upright standing stone used in cultic worship, not a statue or "image".
Hebrew shachefet and qaddachat are a wasting illness and a fever; "consumption" (tuberculosis) and "ague" (malarial fever) are specific older diagnoses read into general terms.
Hebrew nechushah is copper or bronze; brass (a copper-zinc alloy) was not in use, and in 1611 "brass" covered copper alloys generally.
Hebrew hammanim, now known from inscriptions and finds to be small incense altars (possibly linked to the sun, chammah); the KJV's "images" was a guess.

kjv: they (the Israelites) then accept of the punishment of their iniquity
mine: they (the Israelites) then make amends for their iniquity
note: Hebrew yirtsu et-awonam, from ratsah "be pleased with / pay off"; the same verb is used of the land "enjoying/paying off" its sabbaths (v. 34), so the sense is paying off the debt of guilt, whether as "accepting punishment" or "making amends" (also v. 43).
